newsitem.title: CANADA: Ag Canada sees 1997/98 grain, oilseed prices slip.
newsitem.headline: Ag Canada sees 1997/98 grain, oilseed prices slip.

text.p: Agriculture Canada said Tuesday 1997/98 (Aug/July) grain and oilseed prices should fall despite a cut in cereal output due to drought stress.

"Expected yields in western Canada of wheat, barley and durum, in particular, have been revised downward because of heat and drought stress in July in the southern part of the Prairies," the Ag Canada supply and disposition report stated.

World output of wheat, coarse grains and oilseeds were expected to be at or near record levels which should weigh on 1997/98 crop year prices. Except for durum, grain and oilseed prices in Canada were forecast to drop from 1996/97 levels.

"If North American spring wheat crop is smaller than expected, dryness continues in Australia and the European Union does not begin an aggressive export program, the price outlook could improve," Ag Canada said.

Domestic crush demand for canola was expected to rise as prices decline from their 1996/97 level. Exports were expected to be similar to 1996/97 but below earlier forecasts because of uncertainty over whether the EU will approve transgenic canola seed imports.
Barley exports were expected be high but below the 1996/97 record due to low US and North African output.
